concepts.label: Bi-directional XDCR between mobile clusters (Sync Gateway 4.0+)
Eventing/XDCR replication loop
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the specific failure mode this whole page is about (an Eventing function's own write re-triggers itself via active-active XDCR, never terminating); no existing concept names this pattern, though eventing:recursive-mutation is a related-but-distinct SINGLE-cluster hazard (a function's own write landing back in the same keyspace it listens to) rather than this page's cross-cluster, XDCR-mediated version

relations.subject: eventing:replication-loop
relations.evidence: Eventing functions deployed on both ends of this replication topology must avoid reprocessing updated documents in a way that causes XDCR to ping-pong and never stop replicating.

relations.subject: eventing:replication-loop
relations.evidence: One way to avoid loops is to check whether the document has already been enriched.

relations.subject: eventing:on-update-handler
relations.evidence: A better solution introduces a per-cluster ID (e.g., `DC1`, `DC2`) to conditionally apply transformations.

relations.subject: sgw:bidirectional-xdcr
relations.evidence: Without proper logic, Eventing functions in active-active XDCR environments may create infinite loops that consume excessive resources and destabilize the system.

relations.subject: eventing:replication-loop
relations.evidence: These issues apply to all Couchbase versions with Eventing and XDCR support, and are now relevant with Sync Gateway 4.0 support for Bidirectional XDCR.

notable_absence.finding: The page's closing recommendation list (State Checks, location-based rules, Single-Cluster Deployment, Dedicated Buckets, External Transformations) names five distinct mitigation STRATEGIES for the same hazard, but only the two demonstrated in worked code examples (field-presence check, cluster-identifier check) were extracted as relations - the other three (Single-Cluster Deployment, Dedicated Buckets, External Transformations) are one-line bullet mentions with no example or further detail to quote a load-bearing evidence sentence from beyond the bullet itself.

cross_product_finding: This page is Eventing documentation (case_2_enrich_ips, based on server/current/eventing/eventing-example-data-enrichment.md) reused wholesale as a Sync-Gateway-server-compatibility page purely because the hazard it describes becomes newly relevant once Sync Gateway 4.0 makes active-active XDCR available to mobile deployments - the underlying Eventing mechanism (eventing:recursive-mutation, eventing:on-update-handler) is unchanged from server/'s own documentation of it; only the framing and the closing paragraph's cross-reference to Sync Gateway 4.0 are new content specific to this batch.
